The lining of the digestive tract (including the epithelial lining of the gut and associated organs like the liver and pancreas) and the respiratory tract (epithelial lining of the airways) both derive from the endoderm.  
The mesoderm gives rise to connective tissue, muscle, and other supportive structures, but not the epithelial lining itself in these tracts.  
The ectoderm forms the epidermis and nervous system, not the internal linings of the digestive or respiratory tracts.  

Final answer: (A)
